BiblicalUsage: gôwlâh is a plain word for exile, captivity, exiles. In 1 Chronicles 5:22, the text says "because the war [was] of God. And they dwelt in their steads until the captivity." In Nehemiah 7:6, the text says "that went up out of the captivity."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe gôwlâh shows us that hope is not wishing; it is trusting God for what He has promised, even before we see it. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile
